<p dir="auto">If the default were off and you had to set an environment variable to turn it on, they would get no data, because nobody cares enough one way or the other to do anything about it at all.</p>

<p dir="auto">Well, they would get data from those users that value the product and want to help make it better (like me). class="markdown-body" data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body safe-html-box__Uwc6Al"><p dir="auto">Everyone should take a step back and think what this is about - for me its about saying it's NOT ok to yet another step towards complete lack of any privacy, since "it's OK". Yet it might or might not be, the key problem is that companies push it every year slightly further and further, and if everyone won't stand against it - it will be OK at some point that your insurance company, bank, creditor or law firm tells you they can't offer you some service (since some algorithm somewhere put you in the pile of risky clients, but they wont tell you that). It's already happening all around- it might not happen to you in a month or year, but at some point it will. Just think about the amount of digital footsteps we leave each day behind.</p>
<p dir="auto">Therefore I don't want Microsoft to gather any kind of data about anything WITHOUT MY EXPLICIT CONSENT. It's not OK and let's focus on this please!</p>
<p dir="auto">I strongly advise anyone who might think "I don't have anything to hide" to read about BigData related ethics and the issues involved. By the end of the day any kind of output is a prediction - but no one cares and takes the same prediction for granted - the same prediction might misleadingly or unjustly categorize YOU in a harmful manner - this is the issue for me. You might think - but how? Simply, by the data every company is gathering about you - since it's OK. Think about it.</p>
<p dir="auto">If we all just stand by and say "It's ok" then companies will push this further and further.</p></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex gap-1 flex-wrap"><div data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body safe-html-box__Uwc6Al"><p dir="auto">I installed .net core today and the telemetry option was not opt-in. Clearly a violation of GDPR since the data that is shared includes <a href="https://www.eugdpr.org/gdpr-faqs.html" rel="nofollow">personal information </a></p>
<p dir="auto">edit<br>
Wow, what I thought to be an innocent comment got way more attention than it should. Just to clarify, I did not intend to start an anti-Microsoft campaign, I simply wanted to report the issue through what I assumed to be the most appropriate channel.</p>
<p dir="auto">The .net core documentation <a href="https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/tools/telemetry" rel="nofollow">page </a> states that (among other stuff) this data is collected</p>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto">Hashed MAC address: a cryptographically (SHA256) anonymous and unique ID for a machine. This metric is not published.</p>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto">The FAQ page of the EUGDPR.org website states: (note emphasis mine)</p>
<blockquote>
<h2 dir="auto">What constitutes personal data?</h2>
<p dir="auto">The GDPR applies to ‘personal data’ meaning any information relating to an identifiable person who can be directly or indirectly identified in particular by reference to an <strong><em>identifier</em></strong>. This definition provides for a wide range of personal identifiers to constitute personal data, including name, identification number, location data or <strong><em>online identifier</em></strong>, reflecting changes in technology and the way organisations collect information about people.</p>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto">The way I interpret this, an <strong><em>identifier</em></strong> based on the MAC address of the PC where the SDK is installed is considered personal data and hence the data collection should follow the guidelines from the GDPR regulations.</p></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex gap-1 flex-wrap"><div class="ReactionPopoverAnchor__B84pko"><button I will not install Windows on principle because I know it's loaded with your pushy telemetry as well. <p dir="auto">It does not take a lot of effort on your part to make the choice opt-in rather than opt-out by default, and no argumentation that project contributors or anyone else made in this thread or others of this type (there are a couple issues on here if I remember correctly about the topic of telemetry) have clearly been able to show why doing so would somehow compromise your product feedback.</p>
<p dir="auto">So listen to your users who are clearly speaking out against this telemetry (or rather the way you choose to context the collection of it). All you have to do is make it compliant to their expectations, because that's what building great user experiences is all about. I don't get why this is so hard to understand.</p>
<p dir="auto">These telemetry GH issues demonstrate that people are passionate about your product and about their own privacy.
